root_cause.text: A time-of-check-time-of-use race window exists where a netdev reference is acquired in the pre-callback but the hierarchy lock (netdev instance lock) is taken later in the callback body, so the device can be unregistered and its hierarchy flushed between these two points, allowing a new hierarchy to be allocated after flush and causing a memory leak.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description states: "The netdev may get unregistered in between the time we take the ref and the time we lock it. We may allocate the hierarchy after flush has already run, which would lead to a leak." The patch moves the acquisition of the instance lock (via `netdev_get_by_index_lock`) into the pre-callback (`net_shaper_ctx_setup_lock`) and removes the separate `net_shaper_lock`/`net_shaper_unlock` from the doit handlers, ensuring the lock is held from the start of the operation.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove unused static helper functions `net_shaper_lock` and `net_shaper_unlock` to clean up code.
intent_record.what: Removed two static functions `net_shaper_lock` and `net_shaper_unlock` that contained switch statements to call `netdev_lock` and `netdev_unlock` for `NET_SHAPER_BINDING_TYPE_NETDEV`.
intent_record.how: The functions are no longer defined; any code that previously called them will now fail to compile unless the callers have also been removed or adapted. The removal indicates that the locking mechanism via these wrappers is no longer needed.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add locked variants of the net_shaper context setup and cleanup functions to properly serialize write handlers by acquiring and releasing the net_device lock.
intent_record.what: Added two new functions: net_shaper_ctx_setup_lock() which acquires the net_device lock after validating attributes and existence of net_shaper_ops; and net_shaper_ctx_cleanup_unlock() which releases that lock. These mirror the existing net_shaper_ctx_setup() and net_shaper_ctx_cleanup() but include explicit locking/unlocking instead of reference counting.
intent_record.how: For write handlers (non-dump), the new setup function uses netdev_get_by_index_lock() to both look up the net_device and acquire its lock, returning with the lock held. If the device lacks net_shaper_ops, it unlocks and returns an error. The cleanup function net_shaper_ctx_cleanup_unlock() releases the lock via netdev_unlock() when the binding type is NETDEV. This ensures that write operations hold the net_device lock for the duration of the operation, preventing concurrent modifications.

intent_record.intent_summary: Clarify the locking assumption in the comment for `net_shaper_hierarchy_setup`.
intent_record.what: Updated the comment in `net_shaper_hierarchy_setup` to specify that it is called under the lock protecting the hierarchy (instance lock for netdev) instead of the net shaper lock.
intent_record.how: No functional change; only the comment text was modified to describe the correct locking context.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add pre_doit and post_doit hooks for write operations in net_shaper netlink interface to acquire and release write locks.
intent_record.what: Added two new functions: net_shaper_nl_pre_doit_write and net_shaper_nl_post_doit_write. The pre function sets up a write lock using net_shaper_ctx_setup_lock with NET_SHAPER_A_IFINDEX attribute, and the post function cleans up the lock with net_shaper_ctx_cleanup_unlock.
intent_record.how: These functions are intended to be used as pre_doit and post_doit hooks for write operations in the net_shaper netlink family. They ensure that write commands acquire an exclusive lock before processing and release it afterward, providing proper synchronization for write-side operations.

bic_trace_step.reason: The commit introduces `net_shaper_nl_set_doit` and `net_shaper_nl_delete_doit` which first obtain the binding via `net_shaper_binding_from_ctx(info->ctx)` (line 597 in set, line 685 in delete) and only later acquire the hierarchy lock via `net_shaper_lock(binding)` (line 599 in set, line 687 in delete). This creates a TOCTOU race window: between the pre-callback (which sets up the binding without holding the lock) and the doit locking, the net_device can be unregistered and its hierarchy flushed. The subsequent `net_shaper_hierarchy_setup` allocates a new hierarchy, causing a memory leak when the old hierarchy is freed without the new one being cleaned up. The fix would require holding the lock before obtaining the binding or taking a reference to prevent unregistration, neither of which is present.
